title: Ancient Bird With Dinosaur Teeth May Have Lost the Power to Fly
summary:
A crow-sized fossil found in China is changing the story of how birds evolved. The 150-million-year-old creature, named Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, lived in the Late Jurassic period, about 150 to 148 million years ago. Researchers say it may be the earliest known bird lineage to lose the ability to fly.

That is a surprise. Many people picture early birds steadily becoming better flyers. This fossil suggests early birds were already trying out different ways of life, including life on the ground.

The fossil was found in the Zhenghe Fauna of Fujian Province in southeastern China. Yuezhuornis mixes bird and dinosaur features. It had bird-like pelvic and hindlimb structures, but its jaws held closely spaced, serrated teeth like those of deinonychosaurs, small meat-eating dinosaurs related to birds. Its second toe could bend backward unusually far and carried a curved, sickle-shaped claw.

Scientists compared its anatomy in two ways, maximum parsimony and Bayesian tip-dating. Both put Yuezhuornis within Avialae, the group that includes modern birds and their closest extinct relatives, just beyond Archaeopteryx and as a close relative of Zhengheornis. Its limb proportions resembled modern ground-dwelling birds, suggesting it lived on the ground and was likely unable to fly.
why_it_matters: It shows that evolution is full of surprises, and even animals you think you know can change in unexpected ways.
